notes: Active ownership is determined only by a successfully created exclusive-scope lock.
Claiming does not change task status.
Tasks were seeded from the Premium Indie Gap Analysis dated 4 October 2026 and current player-feedback defects.
Tasks are role-owned through primary_agent. Agents normally claim only tasks assigned to their own agent number unless Josh explicitly reassigns the work or the queue is updated.
Supporting agents may advise or review but must not independently implement the primary task without a separate non-overlapping queued scope.
Agent 6 — The Warden is a black-box QA/playtest role. It may create QA reports and non-duplicate follow-up tasks, but should not implement specialist feature fixes inside QA tasks.
Warden findings must include reproduction steps/evidence, severity, player impact and the recommended owner agent. Check the existing queue before creating a new task.
Small PR policy: one claimed task/scope per PR; avoid unrelated refactors. Split broad work into follow-up tasks instead of creating giant integration PRs.
Subjective quality policy: agents may report evidence about clarity, pacing, repetition and friction, but Josh is the creative director and final judge of fun/premium feel.
All black-box Warden QA must drive a real browser (Playwright, agent-browser or equivalent). Reading source/DOM alone is not a playtest.

Agent 7 — The Director owns design governance, not specialist implementation. It reviews work against docs/VISION.md, docs/DECISIONS.md and canonical terminology, flags cross-task conflicts, and proposes queue/dependency corrections.
Josh remains final creative director. The Director may protect and interpret established pillars but must not materially change product direction without Josh's approval.
Before a specialist feature PR is treated as merge-ready, The Director should perform a design-coherence review and record any blocking conflict or terminology/tone issue in the PR or queue.

tasks.title: Immediate action feedback and meaningful button responses
tasks.goal: Every player-facing action visibly confirms what happened; no button should appear inert when state changes.
acceptance_criteria: Scavenge rope and salvage gives immediate visible feedback and cannot silently repeat unintended rewards.
Rest at the inn gives immediate visible feedback describing time/resource/health effects.
Hear rumours gives immediate visible feedback even when no new rumour is available.
Audit all interactive buttons for a visible success, failure, blocked, or no-op explanation.
Relevant feedback remains readable on phone-sized screens.
tasks.notes: Completed 4 Oct 2026 via PR #1: retained the existing salvage/inn/rumour feedback pass, added explicit feedback for non-adjacent map taps, and added a defensive visible failure for unhandled controls.

tasks.title: Coherent visual identity foundation
tasks.goal: Create a consistent lightweight art/presentation layer without turning the game into a 3D project.
acceptance_criteria: Define reusable visual slots for party/NPC portraits, settlement/site art, enemies and items.
Improve map iconography and state readability.
Add restrained movement/combat/hit/heal/status visual feedback.
Assets degrade gracefully when unavailable and remain performant on mobile.
tasks.notes: Merged in PR #3. Reusable art slots, clearer map iconography, restrained visual feedback, reduced-motion support and docs/ART-DIRECTION.md.

tasks.title: Audio and atmosphere foundation
tasks.goal: Give the Grey March a recognisable audio identity with optional, lightweight browser audio.
acceptance_criteria: Add opt-in/controllable ambience support for weather and key locations.
Add restrained UI/combat feedback sounds.
Persist mute/volume preference.
Respect browser autoplay restrictions and reduced-distraction play.
tasks.notes: Merged in PR #4. Default-off Web Audio atmosphere, weather/location ambience, restrained action cues, persisted sound/ambience/volume controls, autoplay-safe gesture unlocking, and docs/AUDIO-DIRECTION.md.

tasks.title: Make the four heroes into persistent characters
tasks.goal: Turn Garrick, Mira, Oren and Brindle from stat packages into people the player can become attached to.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce persistent character memories/traits or relationship state.
Add camp conversations and reactions to major decisions.
Support friendship/rivalry/loyalty changes without breaking old saves.
Provide hooks for personal quests and character-specific consequences.
tasks.notes: The premium gap analysis identifies personality/emotional weight as the biggest missing ingredient. Completed by Agent 2 on 4 Oct 2026: persistent trust/memories, party bonds, six camp conversations, personal-story hooks and major-decision reactions merged in PR #2.

tasks.title: Visible world and faction consequences
tasks.goal: Make choices visibly alter the Grey March instead of only changing hidden numbers.
acceptance_criteria: At least several existing decisions alter later dialogue, services, routes, danger, settlement state, or faction-specific service/price modifiers.
Faction pricing changes are expressed as documented modifiers/hooks; LR-0005 does not rebalance global base prices or the overall economy.
Faction changes have visible player-facing explanations.
End-of-campaign state can remember named decisions, not only renown/reputation totals.
tasks.notes: Storyteller owns consequence logic and faction-specific modifiers. The Mechanist owns base economy/prices in LR-0016. This task is grandfathered as already in flight but has LR-0011/LR-0013 merge gates. Implementation is complete on commit 5c9e3caf2823b3f84ec548c7cdff58dbda6bad44 and archived draft PR #7. CI coordination validation passed; merge verification is intentionally blocked by LR-0011 and LR-0013. After those gates are DONE, a fresh Agent 2 claimant should create a new claim/branch, rebase or cherry-pick the LR-0005 implementation, run the real-browser harness, obtain fresh Agent 7 Director approval as the final PR commit, then merge.

tasks.title: Meaningful progression and builds
tasks.goal: Add build choices with trade-offs rather than linear stat growth.
acceptance_criteria: Define a small equipment or upgrade model that creates real choices.
Support at least one mutually exclusive upgrade decision per hero or build path.
Allow persistent injuries/conditions or transformations to affect play.
Save/load remains compatible.
tasks.notes: Premium-gap area: progression/builds.

tasks.title: Conditional authored event expansion
tasks.goal: Build memorable conditional travel/camp events that react to the party and prior choices.
acceptance_criteria: Event conditions can react to party members, traits/injuries, weather, factions, items, earlier decisions, time and quest outcomes.
Add a first curated batch of memorable events using those conditions.
Avoid filler events whose only effect is a generic resource roll.
tasks.notes: Blocked until character, consequence and progression foundations exist.

tasks.title: Strengthen the 18-day campaign arc and endings
tasks.goal: Turn the existing 18-day renown frame into a clearer escalating dramatic arc with substantially different endings.
acceptance_criteria: Define early, mid and late campaign beats without removing sandbox freedom.
Add a mid-campaign revelation and escalating faction pressure.
Add a hard late-game decision.
Endings reference specific consequential choices.
tasks.notes: Premium-gap area: campaign arc/replayability.

tasks.title: Phone-native interaction and accessibility pass
tasks.goal: Make Lantern Road feel intentionally designed for a phone browser rather than merely responsive.
acceptance_criteria: Improve one-handed interaction flow and choice sizing.
Verify map panning/zooming/touch targeting.
Add autosave and a clear save-slot direction without data loss.
Provide adjustable text size and high-contrast/accessibility settings.
Consider optional haptic feedback where browser/device support allows it.
The settings gear and any floating/mobile controls never overlap or obscure actionable buttons at supported phone widths, including enlarged text settings.
Expose a visible build/version identifier in an unobtrusive Settings/About surface so stale service-worker/cache builds can be identified during support and testing.
tasks.notes: Premium-gap area: mobile experience. Also owns the reported settings-gear overlap and a visible player/support-facing build/version identifier so stale cached builds are obvious.

tasks.title: Architecture modularisation and integration audit
tasks.goal: After the already-in-flight specialist branches land, split the monolithic runtime/content hotspots into safer module boundaries so the next feature wave does not keep colliding in game.js and content.js.
acceptance_criteria: Map current state, rendering, save, combat, content and UI responsibilities and document the intended module boundaries.
Extract high-collision responsibilities from game.js/content.js into small stable modules or data files without changing player-visible behaviour.
Keep a simple static-browser build; do not introduce a heavy framework or bundler unless a documented decision explicitly approves it.
Define ownership/integration contracts so future tasks can usually touch their specialist module instead of the same monolithic files.
Run the real-browser regression harness after the split and preserve existing saves through the documented migration layer.
Record any deliberately deferred extractions as separate queue tasks rather than growing this PR indefinitely.
tasks.notes: Mandatory next-wave architecture gate. It is intentionally blocked until the four already-active specialist branches land, avoiding a disruptive module split underneath live work.

tasks.title: Save format versioning and migration hardening
tasks.goal: Make save/load resilient as character, progression, consequence and mobile systems evolve.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce an explicit save schema/version identifier.
Add a migration path for older saves rather than assuming the latest state shape.
Validate malformed or partial saves and give the player a useful recovery message.
Preserve current campaign data where safely possible.
Document compatibility expectations for future feature agents.

Gate closure evidence: .agent-coordination/gate-evidence/LR-0011.json must be present, VERIFIED, tied to the exact tested commit and successful CI run, and include Josh's explicit Android phone confirmation before this task may be marked DONE.
tasks.notes: Priority-0 safety gate. Current save-changing feature branches may work in parallel but must not merge until this foundation is DONE. Gate completion is evidence-driven: owner implementation alone is insufficient to mark DONE.

machine_requirements: Commit representative pre-versioning/legacy save fixtures that exercise real older save shapes rather than synthetic empty objects.
Automated migration tests load every committed legacy fixture and verify successful migration into the current schema.
Automated current-version round-trip verifies save -> reload/reopen -> restored campaign state without silent data loss.
Malformed/partial/incompatible save cases fail safely with a player-visible recovery path.
A successful CI workflow run on the exact candidate commit publishes the save/migration test report as an artifact.
human_requirements: Josh loads a legacy/pre-gate save on his Android phone after the candidate build is deployed or otherwise accessible.
Josh confirms the campaign opens and core state is intact enough to continue play.
The evidence record contains Josh's explicit phone-check confirmation; agents must not self-assert this field.

tasks.title: Runtime stability and performance baseline
tasks.goal: Establish a performance and stability baseline so new premium-indie features do not gradually make the browser game unreliable.
acceptance_criteria: Identify obvious repeated rendering/event-listener/timer or state-update hazards.
Check startup, travel, map interaction, modal flow and combat for runtime errors.
Add lightweight development diagnostics where useful without affecting normal play.
Keep mobile-browser performance in mind and record any measurable hotspots.
Turn significant out-of-scope findings into separate queue tasks.
tasks.notes: Steward-owned technical quality task.

tasks.title: Automated gameplay regression harness
tasks.goal: Create repeatable real-browser regression checks for Lantern Road's critical game loops so concurrent agent work can be integrated with confidence.
acceptance_criteria: Use Playwright, agent-browser, or an equivalent real browser engine; DOM/code inspection alone does not count as the regression harness.
Automate new campaign creation, representative travel/action flows, and checks for uncaught browser/runtime errors.
Cover save/load round-trip behaviour through browser storage and a page reload/reopen.
Cover at least one combat flow and one quest/site interaction.
Run the browser suite in CI where practical and document the local command every feature agent should run before PR completion.

Gate closure evidence: .agent-coordination/gate-evidence/LR-0013.json must be present, VERIFIED, tied to the exact tested commit and successful CI run, and include Josh's explicit Android phone confirmation before this task may be marked DONE.
tasks.notes: Priority-0 safety gate. Keep tooling light, but the test must drive a real browser. Gate completion is evidence-driven: owner implementation alone is insufficient to mark DONE.

machine_requirements: Playwright or equivalent launches Lantern Road in a real browser; source inspection alone does not count.
The automated suite exercises new campaign, representative travel/action flow, at least one combat flow, at least one quest/site interaction, and save/reload through browser storage.
The suite fails on uncaught page/runtime errors relevant to the tested flows.
A successful CI workflow run on the exact candidate commit publishes browser test results/artifacts.
The local and CI commands needed to reproduce the run are documented.
human_requirements: Josh opens the candidate build on his Android phone and performs a short smoke test covering launch, starting/resuming play, one map/action interaction, and save/reload.
Josh confirms the tested build behaves correctly enough to close the foundation gate.
The evidence record contains Josh's explicit phone-check confirmation; agents must not self-assert this field.

tasks.title: Premium feature integration and consistency pass
tasks.goal: Integrate and reconcile the first premium-indie feature wave after the specialist foundations are complete.
acceptance_criteria: Audit cross-feature conflicts in UI, state, save data, content and pacing.
Ensure specialist systems feel like one game rather than independent feature patches.
Resolve duplicated patterns and inconsistent terminology/feedback.
Run full regression and phone-oriented smoke checks.
Record remaining premium-gap work as a prioritised second-wave queue.
tasks.notes: Blocked until the first specialist foundation wave is complete.

tasks.title: Tactical combat depth and enemy behaviour
tasks.goal: Make combat decisions substantially more interesting without turning Lantern Road into a grid tactics game.
acceptance_criteria: Different enemy archetypes pursue visibly different tactical priorities rather than sharing near-identical behaviour.
Party actions create meaningful choices around targeting, defence, tempo, status effects and resource use.
Enemy intent or other readable telegraphing gives players enough information to make informed decisions.
Combat avoids obvious dominant-action loops and unnecessary click repetition.
Existing encounters remain completable and save/load is not broken.
tasks.notes: Mechanist-owned. Preserve Lantern Road's compact card/target combat identity; deepen decisions rather than adding a tactical grid.

tasks.title: Economy, supplies and expedition pressure balance
tasks.goal: Make gold, rations, rest, shops and expedition resources create sustained but fair pressure across the 18-day campaign.
acceptance_criteria: Audit income, prices, ration use, rest costs and common resource drains across representative runs.
Reduce trivial infinite-value or obviously bad-value transactions and resource loops.
Make settlement services and purchases create real trade-offs without requiring grind.
Ensure poor early luck does not routinely create an unrecoverable campaign spiral.
Document target balance assumptions so later content can price rewards consistently.
tasks.notes: Mechanist owns base prices, income, costs and resource-pressure balance. Consume LR-0005 faction modifier hooks rather than duplicating consequence logic.

tasks.title: Equipment ecosystem and meaningful itemisation
tasks.goal: Expand LR-0006's equipment/build foundation into a small but expressive item ecosystem with meaningful trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Equipment categories/slots from the progression foundation are used consistently.
Add a curated set of distinct equipment choices rather than straight numerical upgrades.
Items support different hero/build identities and situational strategies.
Rare or powerful items have opportunity costs, constraints or meaningful competition.
Shop, reward and save/load flows correctly support the expanded equipment data.
tasks.notes: Blocked on LR-0006 so it extends rather than competes with the progression foundation.

tasks.title: Persistent injuries, conditions and recovery loop
tasks.goal: Turn the progression foundation's injury/condition hooks into memorable persistent consequences that affect expedition decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact set of distinct injuries/conditions with mechanical and narrative-facing effects.
Conditions can arise from understandable risks rather than arbitrary punishment.
Recovery has meaningful costs, choices or time pressure instead of a single automatic reset.
Party members remain viable; injuries create stories and adaptation rather than routine run-ending snowballs.
Persistence and migration behave correctly through save/load.
tasks.notes: Blocked on LR-0006. This is the full recovery loop, not a duplicate of LR-0006's foundational persistent-state hook.

tasks.title: Encounter variety, elites and signature fights
tasks.goal: Use the deeper combat rules to create encounters that feel authored and mechanically distinct rather than permutations of the same fight.
acceptance_criteria: Create encounter compositions that demand different tactical responses.
Add a small number of elite/signature enemies or fight modifiers with recognisable identities.
Major encounters can use bespoke rules or phases where justified without creating one-off engine fragility.
Difficulty escalation is readable and appropriate to campaign timing.
Encounter rewards and risks remain consistent with economy/progression expectations.
tasks.notes: Blocked on LR-0015 because encounter design should exploit the finished combat-depth vocabulary.

tasks.title: Build viability and whole-system balance pass
tasks.goal: Balance the completed Mechanist systems as one coherent game so multiple strategies remain viable across a full campaign.
acceptance_criteria: Test representative campaigns using materially different hero builds and spending strategies.
Identify and correct dominant, trap and non-functional choices.
Check difficulty, resource pressure and progression pacing across early, mid and late campaign.
Ensure combat rewards, equipment, recovery costs and economy reinforce rather than undermine each other.
Record remaining balance uncertainties and create targeted follow-up tasks instead of endless unscoped tweaking.
tasks.notes: Mechanist capstone task. Blocked until its underlying systems exist.

tasks.title: Baseline full-campaign black-box playtest
tasks.goal: Play Lantern Road as a normal player from a fresh campaign through as much of the 18-day arc as possible and identify the highest-impact failures in fun, clarity, pacing and reliability.
acceptance_criteria: Start from a fresh campaign without relying on internal implementation knowledge.
Record major player decisions, progression, friction points and any point where the next action is unclear.
Capture reproducible bugs, soft-locks, broken states, pacing problems, boring/repetitive stretches and moments that feel especially strong.
Classify findings by severity and player impact.
Check the existing queue before creating non-duplicate follow-up tasks and assign each new finding to the appropriate specialist agent.
tasks.notes: The single intentional early QA pass. Establish a baseline before the foundations change; findings may become stale and must be retested later. Real-browser execution is required.

tasks.title: Every-action and navigation black-box audit
tasks.goal: Systematically exercise every visible player control and navigation path to find inert, misleading, inconsistent or unintuitive interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise top-bar controls, map interactions, tabs, settlement/site actions, dialogue choices, shops, camp, combat and save/load controls.
Identify controls that appear to do nothing, give insufficient feedback, have unclear labels, or produce surprising results.
Record reproducible steps and expected versus observed player-facing behaviour.
Test both successful actions and blocked/no-op states.
Route non-duplicate findings to the appropriate specialist rather than implementing fixes directly.
tasks.notes: QA counterpart to LR-0001/LR-0009; evaluates player experience rather than implementing UI changes. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Save, load and resume destructive playtest
tasks.goal: Try to break campaign persistence through real player save/load/resume behaviour and unusual timing/state combinations.
acceptance_criteria: Save and reload from settlements, travel, sites, dialogue/event states and combat where supported.
Test repeated loads, refreshing/reopening the browser, partial progress and unusual action sequences.
Look for duplicated rewards, lost progress, impossible states, stale UI and corrupted or inconsistent restored state.
Record exact reproduction paths and whether the failure is deterministic.
Create non-duplicate findings for The Steward or relevant specialist; do not repair save internals within the QA task.
tasks.notes: A later release-candidate regression retests persistence after save hardening and feature integration. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Exploit, resource-loop and soft-lock hunt
tasks.goal: Actively attempt to abuse Lantern Road's systems to find infinite resources, repeatable rewards, sequence breaks, unwinnable states and other player-visible exploits.
acceptance_criteria: Try repeated site actions, rest/shop loops, travel/camp loops, save/load abuse and reward re-entry.
Look for infinite gold/rations/items/renown, free healing, repeatable quest rewards and bypassed costs.
Identify soft-locks or states where the campaign remains technically running but meaningful progress is impossible.
Rate exploit severity based on ease, impact and likelihood of accidental discovery.
Route each reproducible non-duplicate finding to the appropriate specialist.
tasks.notes: Deliberately adversarial player testing. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Quest-path and impossible-state audit
tasks.goal: Test quest and site progression for dead ends, contradictory state, unavailable required actions and sequence-sensitive failures.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise different ordering of rumours, quest acceptance, travel, site resolution and faction-facing decisions.
Look for objectives that cannot be completed, completed objectives that remain active, unavailable required NPC/site actions and contradictory journal/state text.
Test revisiting resolved and partially resolved locations.
Record the smallest reproducible state/path for each failure.
Create non-duplicate specialist tasks rather than rewriting quest code directly.
tasks.notes: Focus is state integrity and player completion paths, not authorship. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Fresh-player clarity and onboarding playtest
tasks.goal: Approach Lantern Road as if seeing it for the first time and identify where the game fails to teach goals, controls, terminology, consequences or next steps naturally.
acceptance_criteria: Begin without consulting README/internal documentation.
Record every point where the player's goal, available action, cost, risk or expected outcome is unclear.
Assess information density, jargon, tutorialisation-by-play and whether important systems surface at the right time.
Distinguish genuine confusion from intentional uncertainty or mystery.
Route recommendations to the appropriate specialist without turning the QA task into a redesign implementation.
tasks.notes: Tests intuitiveness rather than raw functionality. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Narrative continuity and consequence playtest
tasks.goal: Play branching narrative paths after the Storyteller foundation is complete and find dialogue, memory, consequence and ending contradictions.
acceptance_criteria: Test materially different decisions and faction alignments.
Look for characters forgetting major events, inappropriate dialogue, contradictory relationship reactions and consequences that fail to surface.
Verify endings acknowledge relevant named decisions and campaign outcomes.
Assess whether consequences feel understandable rather than merely hidden state changes.
Route reproducible findings to The Storyteller or Steward as appropriate.
tasks.notes: Unlocks after the first narrative/consequence/event/campaign wave. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Combat fun, difficulty and tedium playtest
tasks.goal: Evaluate whether the deeper combat system is readable, varied, fair and enjoyable across repeated encounters rather than merely mechanically functional.
acceptance_criteria: Play multiple encounter types using different party/build approaches.
Identify dominant actions, fake choices, difficulty spikes, trivial fights, excessive repetition and unclear enemy behaviour.
Assess perceived battle length and decision density rather than only win/loss outcomes.
Test whether signature/elite encounters actually require different thinking.
Route balance/design findings to The Mechanist with reproducible examples.
tasks.notes: Player-experience validation of Mechanist combat work. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Phone one-handed usability black-box playtest
tasks.goal: Test the completed mobile UX pass as a real phone game and identify interactions that remain awkward, error-prone, cramped or tiring.
acceptance_criteria: Play substantial sessions in portrait orientation using touch only.
Test map tap/pan/zoom, modals, choice cards, combat, scrolling, text sizing and save/resume flows.
Look for accidental taps, obscured controls, reachability problems, tiny targets and excessive scrolling.
Assess one-handed comfort and whether feedback is visible without hunting through logs.
Route findings to The Wayfinder or relevant specialist.
tasks.notes: Independent validation after LR-0009, not a duplicate implementation pass. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Release-candidate regression and quality gate
tasks.goal: Perform an independent functional/player-experience regression after integration and specialist QA. The Warden reports evidence and release risks; Josh makes the final creative-director judgement on fun, premium feel and release readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Run fresh-campaign and resumed-campaign real-browser regression passes across core loops.
Retest previously reported critical/high findings and mark them verified or still reproducible.
Report evidence on stability, clarity, pacing, repetition, character continuity, combat readability, presentation and mobile comfort without claiming an objective measurement of 'fun'.
Create only non-duplicate release-blocking follow-up tasks with explicit severity and owner.
Produce a functional go/no-go recommendation plus a separate creative-signoff section reserved for Josh.
tasks.notes: The Warden's final premium-indie quality gate. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Authored illustration and asset production pass
tasks.goal: Curate, optimise and integrate the approved illustration set into Lantern Road's existing visual slots while keeping mobile download cost controlled.
acceptance_criteria: Select the strongest approved images from LR-0042 and reject inconsistent generations rather than forcing full coverage.
Crop and prepare final party, NPC, settlement, site, enemy and item artwork for the existing art-slot contract.
Compress final assets for phone browsers and choose suitable browser-friendly raster formats.
Integrate assets without changing gameplay logic and retain graceful fallback sigils when any image is unavailable.
Perform a consistency pass for silhouette, palette, crop, contrast and small-screen legibility.
Record final asset filenames and provenance references in the art-direction documentation.
tasks.notes: Second-wave Lamplighter integration task. AI image generation itself is split into LR-0042 to avoid mixing generation with curation, optimisation and repo integration. Blocked until LR-0042 is DONE.

tasks.title: Bespoke soundscape and restrained score production pass
tasks.goal: Replace or augment the procedural audio foundation with a coherent authored soundscape and restrained adaptive score while preserving phone performance and player control.
acceptance_criteria: Produce clean loopable ambience layers for core weather states and the main location families.
Produce a cohesive final UI, travel and combat cue set with controlled loudness and no cue spam.
Add a small restrained set of adaptive musical motifs or stems for road, safety, danger, revelation and late-campaign pressure.
Integrate authored audio through the existing master-volume, mute, ambience and autoplay-safe controls.
Keep procedural audio as a graceful fallback when authored assets are unavailable or fail.
Compress assets for phone browsers, verify clean looping/no clicks, and document source/licence provenance for every asset.
tasks.notes: Second-wave Lamplighter task discovered during LR-0003. This is authored production audio and music, not a duplicate of the browser-audio foundation.

tasks.title: Design governance baseline and terminology bible
tasks.goal: Turn the product vision into a compact working design bible so every agent uses the same pillars, terminology, tone and product boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Review docs/VISION.md and docs/DECISIONS.md for contradictions, ambiguity and missing ownership boundaries.
Create a concise canonical terminology/tone guide covering world, party, factions, UI language, combat/progression vocabulary and naming conventions.
Define what counts as pillar drift versus an acceptable implementation variation.
Record a short design-review checklist that can be applied to every specialist PR.
Do not materially change product direction without explicit approval from Josh.
tasks.notes: Priority-0 Director foundation. Establishes the shared language and review standard; does not implement gameplay features.

tasks.title: Cross-task conflict and dependency audit
tasks.goal: Audit the whole Lantern Road work queue for hidden overlap, contradictory acceptance criteria, shared-file collision risk and missing dependencies before they become merge problems.
acceptance_criteria: Review every non-DONE task against all other active/blocked tasks for overlapping ownership or contradictory goals.
Flag collisions in pricing/economy, save state, terminology, UI presentation, narrative consequence and other shared systems.
Add or adjust dependencies/ownership boundaries only where the conflict is concrete and documented.
Do not duplicate existing tasks; merge or clarify ambiguous scopes instead.
Record important governance decisions in docs/DECISIONS.md.
tasks.notes: Director-owned production/design audit. This is a coordination task, not code refactoring.

tasks.title: First-wave design coherence review
tasks.goal: Review the first specialist wave as one game and identify where individually good features have drifted apart in tone, terminology, player promises or product identity.
acceptance_criteria: Review the merged character, consequence, progression, visual/audio and mobile foundations against all five design pillars.
Check terminology and tone consistency across UI, narrative, system labels and player feedback.
Identify cross-system promises that conflict, duplicate or undermine each other.
Route concrete implementation fixes to the responsible specialist rather than making broad feature changes inside this review.
Escalate genuinely subjective creative-direction decisions to Josh.
tasks.notes: Design review after the foundation wave. Agent 7 diagnoses and routes; specialists implement.

tasks.title: Release design cohesion and scope audit
tasks.goal: Perform the final design/production audit before release candidate sign-off, separating genuine product-identity problems from optional polish and scope creep.
acceptance_criteria: Audit the release candidate against the five pillars, non-goals, terminology guide and decision log.
Identify tone drift, inconsistent terminology, duplicated systems, unresolved task conflicts and features that no longer justify their complexity.
Classify findings as release-blocking coherence issues, post-release polish, or intentional design variation.
Make no claim that the game is objectively fun; present creative trade-offs for Josh's final decision.
Produce a concise final design-cohesion recommendation for Josh.
tasks.notes: Final Director gate. Josh retains final creative sign-off.

tasks.title: Hero-specific personal questlines
tasks.goal: Turn the personal-story hooks for Garrick, Mira, Oren and Brindle into authored side arcs that deepen attachment without bloating the main campaign.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four heroes gets a distinct multi-step personal quest or substantial personal thread unlocked by trust, memories or prior choices.
Each personal arc contains at least one meaningful decision that changes that hero, a party relationship, or a visible world consequence.
Personal arcs reuse the existing character memory/bond system and do not duplicate the main 18-day campaign plot.
Avoid generic fetch-quest structure; each arc must reveal character, create a trade-off, and have a remembered outcome.

Mira's personal arc includes at least one choice whose effect is remembered and surfaces later outside the immediate scene through dialogue, relationship state, world consequence, or ending/campaign callback.
tasks.notes: Follow-up to LR-0004. Distinct from LR-0007 general travel/camp events and LR-0008 main campaign arc. Explicitly tracks the earlier open question of whether Mira's choices carry weight later.

tasks.title: Living NPC dialogue and recurring relationship depth
tasks.goal: Make the Grey March's recurring NPCs feel like people who notice history, faction shifts and the player's reputation rather than static quest dispensers.
acceptance_criteria: Key recurring NPCs gain multiple post-decision or faction-sensitive dialogue states beyond quest acceptance and turn-in text.
Repeated conversations react to named campaign history, faction standing or settlement changes instead of looping one generic line.
Dialogue choices can reveal character, local lore or small narrative consequences without taking over Mechanist economy/balance scope.
The added dialogue is curated and voice-consistent; do not pad the game with interchangeable filler.
tasks.notes: Separate from LR-0005 consequence infrastructure: this is authored social depth using that infrastructure. Separate from LR-0007 event expansion.

tasks.title: Keyboard and screen-reader interaction parity
tasks.goal: Make every critical Lantern Road loop operable and understandable without precise pointer input, including keyboard and assistive-technology use.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard-only players can travel, switch information tabs, use shops, choose dialogue/site actions and complete combat without pointer-only dead ends.
Modal focus enters the active modal, cannot escape behind it unintentionally, and returns sensibly when the modal closes.
Map state, travel alternatives and important status changes expose useful semantic labels and announcements without excessive live-region noise.
Focus order, visible focus treatment and contrast remain clear at Standard, Large and Extra Large text settings.
Reduced-motion and platform accessibility preferences are respected without removing necessary feedback.
tasks.notes: Discovered during LR-0009 after queue de-duplication. This is deeper interaction parity, not a repeat of LR-0009's phone layout/settings work or Warden black-box QA.

tasks.title: PWA install, offline and mobile lifecycle polish
tasks.goal: Make installed and intermittent-connectivity phone play behave like a deliberate app rather than a cached webpage.
acceptance_criteria: Verify installability and manifest/service-worker behaviour on supported Android browsers, including icon/name/theme presentation.
Provide a clear offline state and recovery path instead of silently serving stale or failed content.
Verify background/foreground, reload and interrupted-session behaviour preserves campaign safety through the versioned save layer.
Define cache-update behaviour so a new release does not strand players on an old shell or incompatible asset mix.
Document browser limitations and keep the experience graceful where install prompts or storage are unavailable.

tasks.title: Contextual onboarding and first-run mobile guidance
tasks.goal: Turn fresh-player confusion found by Warden QA into lightweight, replayable phone-first onboarding without front-loading a tutorial wall.
acceptance_criteria: Teach the campaign goal, neighbouring-hex travel, map pan/zoom, save model and primary information tabs through short contextual guidance.
Guidance appears at the moment a system becomes relevant rather than as a long opening manual.
Players can skip, dismiss and later replay help without affecting campaign progress.
Onboarding remains readable and operable with accessibility text sizes, keyboard input and touch.
Coordinate wording with Storyteller-owned narrative content without moving story ownership into this task.
tasks.notes: Discovered during LR-0009. Intentionally depends on LR-0026 fresh-player black-box evidence so implementation responds to observed confusion rather than guessing.

tasks.title: Generate and style-lock the Lantern Road AI art set
tasks.goal: Use ChatGPT image generation to create a coherent original illustration set for Lantern Road, locking a repeatable visual style before production integration.
acceptance_criteria: Generate actual raster artwork, not SVG/CSS placeholders, for the four party heroes first and use them to lock the visual style.
Create a reusable master prompt/style specification covering medium, palette, lighting, framing, texture, mood and prohibited visual drift.
After style approval, generate the major settlements and adventure sites, then enemy archetypes, priority NPCs and priority items.
Keep characters and locations visually consistent across separate generations, regenerating outliers instead of accepting obvious style drift.
Prepare phone-friendly source compositions that remain recognisable at the art-slot sizes defined in docs/ART-DIRECTION.md.
Avoid copyrighted characters, logos or direct imitation of a living artist; keep the setting and visual language original to Lantern Road.
Record prompt/version/provenance metadata for every accepted generation so the art set is reproducible and auditable.
Hand the accepted source images and provenance manifest to LR-0031 for cropping, compression and repository integration.
tasks.notes: Lamplighter image-generation task. This chat/model has image-generation capability and can create the actual artwork. LR-0031 remains the downstream curation, optimisation and integration pass.

agent_roster.name: The Steward
agent_roster.role: Lead, architecture, integration, production discipline, cross-system consistency, bug triage and code review.

agent_roster.name: The Storyteller
agent_roster.role: Narrative, characters, dialogue, quests, consequences, campaign structure and endings.

agent_roster.name: The Mechanist
agent_roster.role: Combat, equipment, abilities, injuries, builds, economy, balance and deeper gameplay systems.

agent_roster.name: The Lamplighter
agent_roster.role: Art direction, UI feedback, animation, map presentation, sound, ambience and overall feel.

agent_roster.name: The Wayfinder
agent_roster.role: Mobile UX, accessibility, save/autosave usability, touch/map behaviour, testing, edge cases and interaction audits.

agent_roster.name: The Warden
agent_roster.role: QA, black-box playtesting and player experience. Repeatedly plays Lantern Road, tries to break it, identifies bugs, exploits, confusion, tedium, pacing and fun problems, and routes reproducible findings back to the appropriate specialist rather than implementing feature fixes.

agent_roster.name: The Director
agent_roster.role: Design direction and production governance. Owns the product vision, terminology and decision log; reviews feature work for pillar alignment, tone/coherence, scope drift and cross-task conflicts; does not replace Josh as final creative director.

foundation_gates.rationale: The ideal architecture/save/test foundations were identified after the first specialist wave had already been claimed. Do not invalidate live work mid-branch. Finish the listed in-flight wave under merge gates, then complete modularisation before new feature work.
